featured_reviews.name: Patricia
featured_reviews.review_text: The Gloria church is an iconic church of Byculla. It is designed in the gothic style of architecture. The building has beautiful stained glass windows and an extremely decorative altar. There are many idols inside as well as an old piano. The church is open to all for free, however there are timings for entry. It is usually open till 10 in the morning and again at 6 in the evening. Make sure to check before going. Also be respectful and do not disturb the peace and sanctity of a religious place when visiting.

featured_reviews.name: Vivek Vetal
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visiting Gloria Church in Byculla, Mumbai felt like discovering a gentle pause button hidden within the city. In a part of Mumbai that is constantly buzzing with movement, people, and stories, the church stands as a serene reminder that beauty doesn’t always shout—sometimes it simply waits for you to notice it.

From the moment I approached the church, I was struck by its quiet dignity. The structure rises gracefully, not trying to overpower its surroundings but still unmistakably commanding attention. Stepping inside, there was an immediate shift in energy. The air felt calmer, almost sacred, as if the space itself encouraged you to slow your pace and lower your voice—not out of obligation, but out of respect.

What stayed with me most was the sense of warmth the church offers. The soft light filtering through the windows, the gentle echo of footsteps, and the stillness of the interiors create an atmosphere that feels deeply personal. Even if you walk in as a visitor with no specific purpose, the space makes you feel welcome. I found myself sitting quietly, absorbing the calm, letting my thoughts settle—something that rarely happens in the rush of everyday life.

There’s a powerful emotional depth in Gloria Church that goes beyond its architecture. You can sense the **generations of faith, hope, and prayer** that have passed through these walls. The church feels lived-in, not in a worn-out way, but in a way that reflects continuity and care. It stands as a witness to countless personal moments—gratitude, grief, joy, and silent reflection.

What I appreciated most is how Gloria Church doesn’t demand anything from you. It simply offers space—space to reflect, to feel grounded, and to reconnect with something deeper, whether that’s faith, history, or inner peace. It’s not just a religious landmark; it’s an emotional anchor in the city.

For anyone exploring Mumbai beyond its usual landmarks, Gloria Church is worth visiting—not just to see it, but to experience it. You leave feeling calmer, more centred, and quietly grateful for spaces that still allow the soul to breathe.

featured_reviews.name: Sagar d
featured_reviews.review_text:
Gloria Church, located in Byculla, Mumbai, stands on one of the oldest Roman Catholic church sites in the city.
2.  The original church, known as Nossa Senhora da Glória, was built in 1632 by Portuguese Franciscans (with some sources crediting the deSouza e Lima family).
3.  It was initially located in Mazagaon and served the community for over three centuries.
4.  The present structure was constructed between 1911–1913 (completed in 1913) in beautiful English Gothic Revival style.
5.  The church features stunning Gothic tracery in stone-carved windows, tall spires, and intricate architectural details inspired by European cathedrals.
6.  It celebrated its centenary (100 years of the current building) in 2013.
7.  The site has a continuous history of worship spanning over 400 years, making it a significant heritage landmark.
8.  The church is famous for its vibrant stained glass windows that create colorful light effects inside during the day.
9.  It underwent major restoration and reopened in 2018, appearing even more magnificent with its 160-feet tall structure.
10.  Gloria Church remains an active parish under the Archdiocese of Bombay and is a popular spot for locals and visitors seeking peace and history.
This beautiful church continues to be a symbol of faith and Mumbai’s Portuguese colonial heritage!

featured_reviews.name: Terence Correia
featured_reviews.review_text:
St. Ignatius Church is where my faith, friendships, and fondest memories were all nurtured. It was here that I was baptized, received my First Communion, and was confirmed, milestones that marked the beginning of my spiritual journey. As a child and youth, I was an active part of the Legion of Mary and St. Anthony’s group, served as an altar server, and joined the youth and prayer groups. I loved helping with church cleaning, decorating the crib, making the Christmas star, and organizing events, all while laughing and playing around the church compound with friends who became like family.

Those days were filled with joy, service, and deep connections, memories I treasure even now. Seeing the church restored to its former glory, after more than 100 years since its foundation, fills my heart with happiness. St. Ignatius Church remains a timeless place of faith, community, and love, where every stone tells the story of generations who have grown, served, and celebrated here.

featured_reviews.name: Vivek Vetal
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visiting St. Thomas Cathedral in Fort, Mumbai felt less like ticking off a heritage checklist and more like stepping into a quieter, more reflective version of the city—one that still breathes calmly despite the chaos outside. Tucked amidst the rush of office-goers, traffic signals, and colonial-era buildings, the cathedral stands with a grace that doesn’t demand attention, yet effortlessly commands respect.

What struck me first was the sense of calm the moment I entered the premises. The noise of Fort seemed to fade instantly, replaced by a soft stillness that felt almost therapeutic. It’s rare to find such a space in South Mumbai where time seems to slow down, inviting you to pause, observe, and simply be present. The cathedral isn’t just visually beautiful; it has an emotional weight to it—one that gently nudges you towards introspection.

The architecture is understated yet powerful. There’s no excessive ornamentation, but every element feels purposeful. The high ceilings, elegant arches, and stained-glass windows allow natural light to pour in, creating an atmosphere that feels warm and welcoming rather than intimidating. As sunlight filters through the glass, the interiors take on a soft glow, making it an ideal place to sit quietly, even if only for a few minutes.

What I appreciated most was how alive the space feels, despite its age. This isn’t a museum frozen in time; it’s a living landmark that continues to serve as a place of worship, community, and history. Reading the plaques and memorials, you’re reminded of the countless lives and stories that have passed through these walls—stories of colonial Bombay, changing times, and enduring faith.

St. Thomas Cathedral is not just for those interested in religion or history. It’s for anyone seeking a moment of calm, a connection to Mumbai’s layered past, or simply a peaceful corner to gather their thoughts. Every visit leaves you a little lighter, a little calmer, and with a renewed appreciation for the quieter, soulful side of the city.

featured_reviews.name: Foodieextreme Foodieextreme
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited July 15, 2025 – Day 12 in India

After visiting the Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Vastu Sangrahalaya museum, our guide brought us to St. Thomas Cathedral—a beautiful and deeply historic church nestled in the heart of Mumbai. Built in the early 1700s, it’s the city’s oldest Anglican church and feels like a peaceful sanctuary surrounded by history.

What took me by surprise were the many graves laid directly into the floor. I made sure my husband and our daughters, ages five and seven, were careful not to step on any. My girls noticed a small white grave and were curious if it belonged to a child. When we read the inscription, we saw that it was for a 54-year-old woman, the wife of an officer. That moment sparked quiet reflection and curiosity in all of us.

Inside, we saw the seat where Mother Teresa had once sat, which was marked with a small plaque. Nearby were two elegant seats once used by King George V and Queen Mary during their visit in 1911. My husband and daughters loved the experience of sitting in those very seats, imagining what it must have been like over a century ago.

What I personally loved most was the peace I felt in the church. Before this trip, many people had asked me to pray for them, knowing this journey was meaningful to me on a spiritual level. In the stillness of the cathedral, I took time to sit quietly and pray for each of them. It was a heartfelt and emotional experience.

We left with calm hearts and lasting memories. I truly loved this visit.

featured_reviews.name: ANIMESH SHUKLA
featured_reviews.review_text:
St. Thomas’ Cathedral is one of Mumbai’s most historic and beautiful churches, offering a serene escape in the bustling Fort area. Built in 1718, it is the oldest Anglican church in Mumbai and an essential part of the city's colonial heritage. The church, now part of the Church of North India (C.N.I.), is not just a place of worship but also a significant historical monument.

Historical Importance: As Mumbai’s first Anglican church, St. Thomas’ Cathedral played a crucial role in the city's colonial past. It was built during British rule and remains a testament to the city's rich history.
Stunning Architecture: The church features classic Neo-Gothic and colonial architectural styles, with elegant arches, stained glass windows, and intricate carvings that transport you back in time.
Peaceful Ambience: Despite being in the heart of the bustling Fort area, the church’s interiors are calm and soothing, making it a perfect place for reflection and prayer.
Well-Preserved Memorials: The walls of the cathedral are adorned with memorial plaques dedicated to British soldiers and officers, offering a glimpse into Mumbai’s past.
UNESCO Recognition: The cathedral is a part of the Victorian Gothic and Art Deco Ensemble of Mumbai, which has been recognized as a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

Visiting Experience
Best Time to Visit: Morning hours are ideal for a quiet and spiritual experience. The church is open to visitors on most days.

Surroundings: Located near Horniman Circle, it is close to landmarks like Flora Fountain, Bombay High Court, Rajabai Clock Tower, and the Asiatic Library.

Mass Timings: If you wish to attend a service, check their schedule beforehand, as Sunday Mass is particularly special.

Photography: While photography is allowed in most areas, it’s best to be respectful as it is an active place of worship.

St. Thomas’ Cathedral is a must-visit for history buffs, architecture lovers, and anyone looking for a moment of peace in Mumbai’s fast-paced environment. Whether you admire its heritage, attend a service, or simply enjoy its quiet beauty, this cathedral is truly a hidden treasure in Mumbai.

featured_reviews.review_text:
This church isn’t just another place of worship — it’s one of the oldest in Mumbai, with origins that trace back over 400 years to the Portuguese Franciscan era. The original structure has been rebuilt multiple times, and the current building — completed in the 1970s — was redesigned by renowned architect Charles Correa, giving it a distinctive, almost modernist architectural character that sets it apart from traditional church designs. There’s even a special skylight in the baptistery designed by celebrated artist M.F. Husain, adding an artistic touch to the sacred space.

Visitors and worshippers consistently describe the church as a peaceful and reflective haven, providing a calming contrast to the busy streets outside. Many find the quiet interiors, gentle lighting, and sense of reverence deeply moving — whether they’ve come to pray or simply to sit in contemplation.

Inside during Mass, there’s often a beautiful choir and uplifting biblical artwork, which many visitors highlight as especially moving. The church’s atmosphere is welcoming to both regular parishioners and first-time visitors.

Conveniently located just a short walk from Dadar station, it’s easy to visit whether you’re a local or a traveller exploring the city’s heritage sites. The church also serves as a well-known landmark in the neighbourhood, sitting comfortably among the vibrant life of Dadar West.

Our Lady of Salvation Church is much more than a place of worship — it’s a living piece of Mumbai’s cultural and architectural history. Whether you’re drawn by its spiritual significance, curious about its design, or simply seeking a quiet moment amidst city life, it’s a highly recommended stop in Dadar.

Whether you’re attending Mass or simply stopping by for a quiet moment, this church offers a sense of calm amidst the busy city life. A wonderful landmark of faith and heritage in the heart of Mumbai.

featured_reviews.name: bhavin rathod
featured_reviews.review_text:
The church is very close to highway near sidhhivinayak temple ....and around 10 -15 min from dadar railway station.
I love the structure of the church and the area in which it is spread is very beautiful.
The entrance of the church is also too beautiful.
